# Typst

For Typst the extension prints each index with page locators, in two columns,
built from the same marks every other back-end reads. A declared index that no
mark files in prints nothing, not even its heading. It needs no Typst
package: everything the index uses is written into the document, so nothing is
downloaded when the document compiles.

A page number is known only once Typst has laid out the pages, and the
extension runs before that. So it writes an invisible Typst label at each mark,
and each locator in the index asks Typst for the page of its label while the
document is typeset. A mark in a heading gets its label just after the
heading, so the copy of that heading in the table of contents carries none.

## Where the index goes

Each index goes where your placement marker puts it, and at the end of the
document where no marker names it, in the order your `indexes:` metadata
declares them. See [Placing the index](placing-the-index.qmd). An index starts
on a new page under an unnumbered level-one heading, which Typst lists in the
table of contents. The heading is the title your `indexes:` metadata gives the
index, or its name where you give no title. A document that declares no
`indexes:` gets **Index**, or its language's word for an index where the
extension covers that language. The text after the index starts on a new page
too.

## Entries

The entries are ordered and grouped as in HTML: a `Symbols` group first, then
one group per letter, each under its letter in bold. See [Letter groups in the
HTML index](letter-groups.qmd). A sub-entry is indented under its parent, and
sub-entries nest as deep as you write them.

## Locators

Each locator is the page number as the page shows it. Each one links to its
page.

- Where the page numbering pattern names two counters, such as `1 / 1`,
  a locator prints both, as the page footer does: `5 / 30`.
- A page with no numbering prints its physical page number.
- Several marks of one term on one page print that page once.
- Locators that print the same text print it once, even from different
  pages, as after a page counter reset. That one locator links to the earliest
  of those pages, and it is bold where any of their marks is a principal
  mention.
- The locator of a principal mention is set in bold. Where a principal and an
  ordinary mark of one term share a page, that page's one locator is bold.
- A range prints its opening and closing pages, `12–15`, and links to the
  opening page. Where both ends of a range are on one page, it prints that page
  alone. Where the two ends print the same text, it prints that text alone.
- An entry's locators are ordered by the numbering of their opening pages, as
  the PDF index orders page numbers. Lower roman numbers come first, then upper
  roman numbers, arabic numbers, lowercase letters, uppercase letters, and then
  any other numbering. The first counting symbol of the page numbering pattern
  sets the kind, so `1 / 1` is arabic. A page with no numbering counts as
  arabic, and a numbering function counts as other. Numbers of one kind are
  ordered by the page counter's value, and then by page. So after a page
  counter reset, `1` comes before a `3` from an earlier page.
- A range whose two ends are numbers of one kind, with a higher closing number,
  spans the numbers from its opening number to its closing number. A mark of
  the term on a spanned number of that kind prints no locator of its own, even
  on a page after the range, as after a page counter reset. A principal mention
  there loses its bold. Any other range spans nothing, and a range never
  removes another range.
- Pages you marked separately stay separate: marks on pages 3, 4 and 5 print
  `3, 4, 5`. Only a range you write prints as a range. A mark on the page just
  after a range prints its own locator, `2–3, 4`, where the PDF index prints
  `2–4`.

## Cross-references

A cross-reference prints its word in italics, then its target as plain text,
with no link. The words are `see` and `see also`, your document language's
words where the extension covers that language, or the words you set under
`index-labels:`, which Typst reads for `symbols`, `see` and `see-also`.

The punctuation is fixed: a comma before each locator and before the first
cross-reference, and a semicolon between two cross-references. The
`separator` and `xref-separator` keys of `index-labels:` do not reach the Typst
index.

## Books

Quarto renders a Typst book as one merged document, so the extension sees every
chapter's marks at once, and a range you open in one chapter and close in
another pairs. Books were tested on Quarto 1.10.18. On that version Quarto's
Typst book template does not compile a book whose `book:` metadata has no
`author:`.

## A mark Typst never prints

A mark in a front-matter field that Quarto's Typst template does not print,
such as `description:`, has no label on any page. Its term is still in the
index, with no page number.
